newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 15.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Following the release yesterday of a significant increase in the AMP Society's profit to A$2.1 billion for 1996, managing director and chief executive George Trumbull predicted the company's retained earnings would increase from A$7.8 billion to approximately A$9 billion by the end of 1997. Page 1.

The four big petrol retailers - Mobil, BP Australia, Shell Australia and Ampol parent company Australian Petroleum Ltd - are gearing up to battle for a stake in the lucrative $A21 billion fresh food market in an attempt to offset a disastrous year in petrol margins. The retailers have plans for new sites housing outlets for convenience stores, liquor and dry-cleaning businesses, fast food and other franchises. Page 6.

After another strong quarterly performance underpinned by food and general merchandise operations, retailer Woolworths is on track to report double-digit earnings growth this year. Consumers have responded strongly to the revamp of the company's clothing lines, particularly within its Big W chain, indicating the downward trend in the apparel sector may have bottomed out. Page 19.

In a deal that would end competition in the rollout of broadband cable, Optus Communications has intensified its efforts to curb the massive losses in pay-TV in an agreement offered to telecommunications rival Telstra. An Optus spokesman said yesterday the deal would sort out pay-TV infrastructure and "eliminate dual overhead cabling and limit the amount of overbuild in the future". Page 19.

A full feasibility study by joint-venture partners in Western Australia's Boddington gold mine has begun on a $A260 million development to keep production of Australia's fourth largest gold mine running well into the next century. Partners Normandy Mining(44.4 per cent), Acacia Resources (33.3 per cent) and Newcrest Mining (22 per cent) have accepted results of a pre-feasibility study and will consider the full report findings at the end of the year. Page 21.

A trend for emerging resource houses to appoint executive chairmen to concentrate on broader issues affecting a company's future could possibly be sparked by the growing complexity of corporate requirements and regulations. Newly appointed Sons of Gwalia Ltd executive chairman Peter Lalor said yesterday he considered it vital that the head of a company was in daily contact with corporate growth and performance. Page 21. --
THE AUSTRALIAN

AMP Society chief executive George Trumbull revealed yesterday that Australia's biggest investor will utilise a A$2.1 billion profit and a growing asset base to pursue an aggressive international growth program ahead of its A$12 billion stock market listig in 1998. Trumbull said AMP was also looking at domestic opportunities, including the possibility of acquiring banking operations. Page 21.

In a result underpinned by economic fundamentals and more attractive stock valuations, the Australian stock market has weathered Friday's 148-point drop in the Dow Jones industrial average, losing only 14.4 points, or 0.6 per cent, to close at 2366.1 yestrday. Page 21.

Speaking after the release of the AMP Society's annual report yesterday, managing director George Trumbull said the company expects continued instability in global investment markets this year, but is confident the year-end investment result will not have an overly negative impact on its worldwide A$94.5 billion portfolio. Page 21.

Speaking at an Australian Institute of Company Directors lunch in Sydney yesterday Foster's Brewing Group chairman John Ralph, arguably Australia's foremost company director, criticised institutional investors in retail giant Coles Myer Ltd for selling down their shareholdings soon after taking collective action to reshuffle the board in 1995. Page 21.

Brian Powers, the managing director of Kerry Packer's Consolidated Press Holdings, issued a statement last night defending the company's role in a controversial 1991 deal involving Australian National Industries Ltd and its purchase of European waste manaement business ABT. CPH threatened to sue Four Corners following a report on Monday April 7 which indicated the deal may have breached the Corporations Law and Australian Stock Exchange listing rules. Page 23.

Speaking at a function to mark the completion of their Jasuraus joint-venture undersea cable to Indonesia, Optus chief executive Ziggy Switkowski and Telstra chief executive Frank Blount indicated the two telecommunications giants are considering plans to share their A$8 billion cable network to prevent further duplication, but have not yet reached an agreement. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Speaking after the release of the AMP Society's annual report yesterday, chief executive George Trumbull said a positive A$2.1 billion profit in 1996 has cleared the way for the company's policyholders to be allocated around A$9 billion in retained profit as shares. Trumbull said policyholders would know by July how many shares they would be entitled to receive from the demutualised group. Page 27.

An article in the Reserve Bank of Australia's monthly bulletin, the RBA's Small Business Finance Advisory Panel, has supported calls for the banks to provide a better deal for small business requiring borrowings, suggesting that the provision of finance to small firms still has room for improvement. Page 27.

In a bid to stave off some of the criticism regarding the A$2.47 million received in 1996 by its managing director George Trumbull, the AMP Society has provided more details than ever on why it pays Trumbull so much and how it rewards other senior staff for performance. Trumbull's income places him as one of Australia's highest paid executives. Page 27.

Optus chief executive Ziggy Switkowski revealed yesterday Optus Vision and national carrier Telstra are considering a plan to co-operate over the roll-out of their cable networks, a proposal he says has the potential to eliminate duplication of aerial fil and could help resolve problems with Australia's pay-TV infrastructure. Page 29.

Bill Beerworth and Linda Nicholls, two members of the five-person committee overseeing the Federal Government's Wallis inquiry into the financial system, said yesterday the tax system was having a negative impact on the regional competitiveness of Australa's financial system, and called on Federal Treasurer Peter Costello to urgently address the system's distortions. Page 29.

Jailed former Perth entrepreneur Alan Bond and John Lord, the liquidator of Bond's family company, Dallhold Investments, have failed to keep a confidential and detailed report on the allegedly hidden overseas assets controlled by Bond out of police hands ollowing a Federal Court decision. The Australian Federal Police will now have access to Lord's lengthy report. Page 29.
THE AGE

Thanks largely to a one-off A$479 million gain from an actuarial reappraisal of its British life office Pearl Group, the AMP Society - Australia's largest life insurer - has posted a better-than-expected A$2.1 billion profit for 1996 as it approaches a A$ billion share give-away in the second half of 1998. Page B1.

According to a study of small business lending in the Reserve Bank's April Bulletin, banks are charging small business average interest rates almost a third higher than those paid by big business - a result which explains why Prime Minister John Howard an Treasurer Peter Costello have demanded the banks provide a better deal for small firms. Page B1.

Two of Australia's big six law firms, Minter Ellison and Blake Dawson Waldron, have been holding merger talks for the past months which, if successful, would create a legal colossus encompassing more than 240 partners and 3,500 staff, making it the largest legal practice in this country. Page B1.

The Australian sharemarket yesterday defied expectations of a slump similar to the 140-point, or two per cent, drop on the United States Dow Jones Industrial Average on Friday, with the All Ordinaries Index losing only 14.4 points to 2366.1 after dropping 30 points shortly after trade opened. Page B1.

The development of the gold-copper resource at Boddingtnon gold project in Western Australia's Darling Ranges beneath existing open-cuts has been priced at $A260 million, plus or minus 20 per cent. Partners Normandy Mining, Acacia Resources and Newcrest have, despite implied high costs, commissioned a full feasibility study of the development. Page B3.

The award of long-anticipated and highly rated exploration leases next to the large Cornea oil discovery off Western Australia has failed to eventuate despite Federal Resources and Energy Minister Warwick Parer being widely tipped to announce the winning permit bidders at the opening of the APPEA conference yesterday. However, Parer did announce the release of 34 new offshore permits. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
